title: Moscow & Anti-Open Lines
intro: Meet 3.Bb5+ cleanly with ...Bd7 and ...Qxd7, attack 3.c3 with ...Nf6, and punish 4.Qxd4 with ...Nc6.
variation: e2e4 c7c5 g1f3 d7d6 f1b5, e2e4 c7c5 g1f3 d7d6 c2c3, e2e4 c7c5 g1f3 d7d6 d2d4 c5d4 d1d4

steps.text: Instead of opening the centre with 3.d4, White often checks with 3.Bb5+, the Moscow Variation.
Block the check and offer to trade off your bad bishop.
steps.hint: Put your c8 bishop on d7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Bd7 so you keep c6 free for your knight.
steps.ifRight: Trading light-squared bishops solves Black's main Sicilian problem.

feedback.b8d7: 3...Nd7 blocks your c8 bishop and is a bit passive. 3...Bd7 is cleaner.

steps.text: Recapture without blocking your knight or damaging your pawns.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Qxd7 so your b8 knight can develop actively to c6.

feedback.b8d7: 4...Nbxd7 puts the knight on a passive square. Take with the queen.

steps.text: Develop your queen's knight towards the centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nc6 to control d4 and e5.

steps.text: If White tries 5.c4 to set up a Maroczy Bind, fight for d4 at once.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to c6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nc6 (followed by ...g6 and ...Bg7) to target d4.
steps.ifRight: With the light-squared bishops gone, Black enjoys easy play on the dark squares.

lessons.title: Meeting 3.c3
lessons.summary: Hit e4 with 3...Nf6 and avoid the Qa4+ trap.

steps.text: With 3.c3 (the Delayed Alapin), White prepares to push d4 and capture back with the c-pawn.
Attack the e4 pawn at once before White can play d4 comfortably.
steps.hint: Develop your king's knight to hit e4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3...Nf6 so e4 is under immediate fire.
steps.ifRight: White must defend e4 instead of pushing d4 for free.

steps.text: White defends e4 quietly with 4.Be2, setting a little trap.
Do not fall for 4...Nxe4 5.Qa4+. Develop cleanly instead.
steps.hint: Bring out your queen's knight to c6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nc6: taking on e4 walks into 5.Qa4+ winning the knight.
steps.ifRight: Solid and alert: now ...e6 or ...g6 follows.

feedback.f6e4: 4...Nxe4 walks into 5.Qa4+, forking your king and knight.

steps.text: If White plays 4.h3, still watch out for Qa4+ and develop smoothly.
steps.hint: Develop your knight to c6 or prepare ...g6.
steps.ifRight: Black develops smoothly and controls the centre.

steps.text: Against 4.Bd3, challenge White's bishop and centre.
steps.hint: Develop your knight to c6 or fianchetto with ...g6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nc6 (or 4...g6) to keep pressure on d4.

lessons.title: Meeting 4.Qxd4 (Chekhover)
lessons.summary: Chase the queen with 4...Nc6 and win the bishop pair.

steps.text: In the Chekhover Variation, White recaptures with the queen (4.Qxd4) to avoid main-line theory.
Gain a free tempo by attacking White's queen.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nc6 to force the queen to move again.
steps.ifRight: White must spend another move on the queen or bishop.

steps.text: Break the pin and chase or trade the bishop.
steps.hint: Put your c8 bishop on d7.
steps.ifRight: White's bishop is forced to trade on c6.

steps.text: Recapture cleanly to keep your bishop pair and open lines.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Bxc6 so your pawn structure stays intact and the c6 bishop aims at e4.
steps.ifRight: Black has the bishop pair and fast development with ...Nf6.

feedback.b7c6: 6...bxc6 is playable, though 6...Bxc6 activates your bishop and keeps your queenside healthy.
